notes: STAND-IN (read as its own source; it does not confirm the article): Carignan, R. 1980. The role of submersed macrophytes in phosphorus cycling. PhD thesis, Department of Biology, McGill University, Montréal (February 1980). Its introduction says Part II 'is being published in Science'. Part II's abstract (thesis PDF p. 31) is the Science abstract almost word for word. Its results (PDF pp. 38–41): macrophytes grown in the mesotrophic part of Lake Memphremagog (Québec–Vermont) 'obtained all their P from the sediments' — per-species estimates of 94–107 % from the sediments (Tables 3–4, so 'all' means within error of 100 %); plants in the eutrophic part showed 91.6 %, which the author says underestimates the sediment share because of unremovable periphyton; at hypertrophic Rivière du Sud (summer SRP 167 µg/L) sediments supplied at least 71.5 % (whole plants about 70 %). The thesis abstract summarizes: more than 95 % from the sediments at mesotrophic and eutrophic sites, 70 % at the hypertrophic one. It also reports that Myriophyllum released 0.32 µg g⁻¹ h⁻¹ P and periphyton took only 6.5 % of its P from the macrophytes. Recommend citing the Science paper once read (doi above, via a library login), or the thesis alongside it.
